samples.summary: Null `clipboardData` is only tested on the image branch; the text-selection cut/copy path's new guard is untested
samples.evidence: `dispatchClipboard(..., { withData: false })` is used in exactly two tests (line 440 copy-image, line 718 cut-image), both with an image selection and no text selection. The new `const clipboard = e.clipboardData; if (!clipboard) return;` in `handleCut` (text-editor.ts:1242-1245) also guards the *text* path, which is the one that calls `saveSnapshot()/deleteSelection()` — a regression there deletes selected text that reached no clipboard, and no test would notice. Same for `handleCopy`'s text path.
searchedFor: grep 'copy' in packages/docs/test (only editor-read-only.test.ts and copy-integrity.test.ts)

samples.summary: No test that Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+C (format painter) or Alt+C still fall through while an image is selected
samples.evidence: The new absorb condition is `mod && !e.shiftKey && !e.altKey && (key === 'c' || key === 'x')`. text-editor.ts:1022-1024 shows Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+C is the format-painter shortcut. Every shortcut test in copy-integrity.test.ts (`pressCopyShortcut`) sets only metaKey/ctrlKey — there is no case with shiftKey or altKey, so dropping `!e.shiftKey`/`!e.altKey` (which would silently swallow the format painter whenever an image is selected) leaves the suite green.

samples.summary: The production click path into `selectImageInline` (image mousedown) is never exercised; all tests enter via the `selectImageAt` API
samples.evidence: Every image test calls `editor.selectImageAt('b1', 2)`. No test in packages/docs/test dispatches a mousedown over an image (grep for 'mousedown'/'activeElement' in image-selection-overlay.test.ts found nothing). The diff also changed the mousedown handler (editor.ts ~2547) to route through `selectImageInline`; if that call site regressed (e.g. back to setting `selectedImage` without focusing), the read-only focus test at line 420 would still pass because it uses the API entry point.

samples.summary: `expect(editor.getSelectedImage()).toBeNull()` is vacuous in the two stale-selection Delete tests
samples.evidence: `EditorAPI.getSelectedImage` (editor.ts:3693-3704) re-validates against the document and returns null whenever the block is gone or the offset no longer holds an image. In 'Delete deletes nothing when the offset no longer holds an image' (line 651) and 'Delete deletes nothing when a peer deleted the block' (line 674) the document has been rewritten precisely so that this is true, so the assertion holds whether or not `deleteSelectedImageInline` actually cleared the internal `selectedImage`. The neighbouring document assertions are meaningful; only this one adds nothing.

samples.summary: The read-only cut tests pass on a pre-existing guard, not on the code this diff adds
samples.evidence: `handleCut` returns at text-editor.ts:1236-1239 (`if (this.readOnly) { e.preventDefault(); return; }`) before any of the new clipboard/image/table-cell logic runs, so 'a read-only editor cuts nothing' (line 801) and 'a read-only editor cuts nothing out of a cell' (line 930) would stay green even if the new image-cut and cell-slice code were deleted entirely. They are regression guards for old behavior rather than coverage of the change, despite the latter's comment framing it as the #872 cut path.

finding.summary: No test asserts the copy/cut keydown is NOT preventDefault-ed — the exact property the #870 fix depends on
finding.evidence: editor.ts:2298-2299 returns `true` for mod+c/x deliberately *without* calling `e.preventDefault()`, because in a real browser preventDefault on the keydown suppresses the native `copy`/`cut` event and nothing would ever be written (the original #870 symptom). Every test in copy-integrity.test.ts synthesizes the clipboard event by hand (`dispatchClipboard` at line 87, called after `pressCopyShortcut`), so the keydown and the clipboard event are fully decoupled: adding `e.preventDefault()` in the image key handler would keep all 20 tests green while Cmd/Ctrl+C over a selected image silently writes nothing again. `pressCopyShortcut` creates a `cancelable: true` event (line 124-126) but no test ever reads `event.defaultPrevented` on it — contrast the copy-event tests at lines 437/460, which do assert `defaultPrevented`.

verdict.reason: The finding claims no test asserts the copy/cut keydown is left un-preventDefault-ed, but four such assertions exist in the cited file. copy-integrity.test.ts:386-399 is a dedicated test ("the copy shortcut is left uncancelled so the browser still copies") whose sole assertion is `expect(pressCopyShortcut(textarea, 'c').defaultPrevented).toBe(false)` (line 397), and copy-integrity.test.ts:708-716 is its cut counterpart with `expect(pressCopyShortcut(textarea, 'x').defaultPrevented).toBe(false)` (line 714). Lines 412 and 432 assert the same for the either-modifier and read-only cases. These assertions are live, not decoupled from the clipboard-event synthesis: pressCopyShortcut (lines 150-157) dispatches a cancelable keydown on the textarea, which reaches TextEditor.handleKeyDown -> this.imageKeyHandler(e) (text-editor.ts:864) -> the closure at editor.ts:2320, whose mod+c/x branch at editor.ts:2341-2342 returns true without preventDefault. Inserting `e.preventDefault()` there — the exact regression the reviewer says would keep all tests green — would set defaultPrevented to true and fail all four assertions. The reviewer's quoted evidence ("no test ever reads event.defaultPrevented on it") is contradicted by the file itself.
